paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. Ezra didn't just own the Law. He had "set his heart to study the Law of the LORD, to practice it, and to teach its statutes and ordinances in Israel" (Ezra 7:10). Study it, do it, teach it. In that order. A man who teaches what he hasn't practiced is just a guy with a loud mustache and no cookies in the oven, and I would know about the mustache.

Now look at who made the trip work. The king said yes to all Ezra's requests, and the writer tells us why: "for the hand of the LORD his God was upon him" (Ezra 7:6). Ezra says it himself at the end: "Blessed be the LORD, the God of our fathers, who has put into the heart of the king to so honor the house of the LORD in Jerusalem" (Ezra 7:27). Ezra got the silver, the letter and the green light, and he gave the credit to the LORD. Baker, that's how we hold our wins too, with open hands and a thank you.

Then see what Ezra did with all that favor: "I took courage and gathered the leaders of Israel to return with me" (Ezra 7:28). God's hand was on him, and he still had to get up and go. That's your lesson, friend. Make your heart a study-it, do-it, share-it kind of heart, trust the hand that's on you, and take courage for the next step. The story isn't over, so keep that oven warm!
